reviews.title: Compact Beast: Premium SFX Power with Outstanding Reliability and Low Noise
reviews.comment: The Corsair SF1000 (2024) SFX Power Supply shipped incredibly fast and showed up the next day with Prime, which is always a great start. Right out of the box, Corsair’s attention to detail is obvious - excellent packaging and a premium feel throughout. Installation was straightforward, especially with the included SFX-to-ATX bracket, and it fit my L300 case perfectly. Compatibility was spot-on for a compact build, though it’s still smart to double-check cable lengths depending on your setup. Speaking of cables, there are plenty included, they’re nicely sleeved, and they make cable management clean and efficient. Performance-wise, this PSU delivers serious power with rock-solid stability. The 80 Plus Platinum efficiency and 105°C-rated Japanese capacitors translate into excellent reliability, even under heavy loads. The low noise level is another big win - the 92mm PWM fan stays quiet while keeping everything cool. Cybernetics rating this as one of the best SFX PSUs of all time definitely shows here. That said, I’d recommend waiting for deals around the $180 mark with coupons - t’s an absolute no-brainer at that price. Overall, this is a top-tier SFX unit that nails power delivery, reliability, cable management, and ease of installation in a compact form factor.
reviews.author: Amazonian Flier

reviews.title: Gold Standard for SFF Builds
reviews.comment: Built my first SFF gaming PC and the SF1000 was the gold standard so I had to get it. One thing to note (which surprised me) is that corsairs SFX PSUs don't have a native 12v-2x6 connection like other SFX PSU's. It uses dual 8 pin on the PSU side and 12v-2x6 on the GPU side. No difference in performance but something to consider in terms of cable tidiness. Overall happy with the PSU performance and noise levels.

reviews.title: Received a used unit
reviews.comment: I bought this item brand new, shipped and sold directly from Amazon, so I expected a factory-sealed product. Unfortunately, that wasn’t the case. The PSU I received was clearly used — it had the well-known LPN label on the box, which is usually a dead giveaway. On top of that, the box wasn’t shrink-wrapped, and the cables weren’t sealed in their original packaging. Everything was just loose inside, which isn’t what you expect when buying a “new” product. After looking through other reviews, it seems like this isn’t an isolated issue either, which is pretty disappointing for something advertised as brand new. That said, the PSU itself seems solid. It’s clearly a high-end unit — efficient, well-built, and easy to install, with great connectors. No complaints there. I just wish I actually received a new one like I paid for. At this point, I’m going to keep it because I don’t have the time or energy to deal with a return and wait for a replacement, but it’s definitely frustrating. I’d recommend buying from somewhere else if you want to be sure you’re getting a truly new unit.
reviews.author: Brian

reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.comment: HWBusters.com recommended, preforms well, and silent at low and medium loads. Corsair made a very good psu for those looking for a silent build. It has short cables meant for small cases, without cable extensions this is useless for a normal sized tower. So don't make that mistake. Highly recommended.
